focus: Safe integration and confirmation model for mcp-tooling, including sk-design pairing
noveltyJustification: Four of six findings are new governance recommendations and two extend prior Webflow operational facts; a simplicity bonus reflects the consolidated confirmation model while staging, idempotency, and universal-pagination gaps remain open.
keyQuestions: Q5: What safe integration and confirmation model follows for mcp-tooling, including sk-design pairing?
answeredQuestions: Q5 substantially: action classification, confirmation gates, sk-design pairing, secret handling, retry posture, and explicit unresolved gaps
ruledOut: Live Webflow MCP discovery, tool invocation, OAuth handshakes, credential use, mutation, publish, and deployment testing
Assuming Beta is an isolated staging environment or assuming universal idempotency/replay/pagination guarantees
Automatic replay of non-idempotent writes and automatic publish-after-write

summary: Remote MCP is OAuth-governed, permission-bounded, activity-logged, and has a documented Bridge App boundary; Beta is not documented as staging.
Publishing is a separately gated deployment boundary with sites:write, explicit domains, 202 acceptance, one successful queue per minute, and all-staged-change blast radius.
Local mcp-tooling and sk-design conventions separate transport evidence from mutation and design judgment.
Adopt read-only, draft/write, destructive, publish, and deployment classes with progressively stronger confirmation and explicit rollback/read-back evidence.
Fail closed on staging, idempotency, and replay gaps; honor Retry-After, avoid blind replay after ambiguous writes, and keep secrets out of packet/config/log output.
Require tool-specific pagination metadata and version-aware preflight; do not promote CMS offset behavior into a universal pagination contract.

name: no-live-webflow-actions
detail: No Webflow tools, credentials, OAuth handshakes, mutations, publish calls, or deployment actions were used.
